newsitem.title: USA: TELE-COMMS TO INVEST IN ASCENT ARENA.
newsitem.headline: TELE-COMMS TO INVEST IN ASCENT ARENA.

text.p: Tele-Communications Inc's Liberty Media Corp will invest $15 million in Ascent Entertainment Group Inc's arena project in Denver, the companies said Wednesday.

Yesterday, Ascent and the city of Denver announced an agreement for Ascent to build, own and operate a $165 million arena near the city center and keep its two professional sports teams -- the Denver Nuggets of the National Basketball Association and the Colorado Avalanche of the National Hockey League -- in Denver for 25 years.

Local media reports said the deal with Liberty Media was aimed at enabling Ascent to pay $15 million to retain hockey superstar Joe Sakic. The New York Rangers have offered Sakic a three-year, $21 million contract.
An Ascent spokesman said the company was not commenting on those reports.
Ascent was to announce later today whether it will match the Ranger offer and thus retain Sakic as Avalanche team captain.
Liberty Media's investment will be in Denver Arena Co LLC, which will build the Pepsi Arena. Neither TCI nor Liberty will be involved in managing or operating the arena.

Ascent and FOX Sports Rocky Mountain, a 50-50 partnership between Liberty Media and News Corp, announced today the signing of a seven-year regional television license agreement for the Nuggets and the Avalanche.
The partnership reaches more than 2.7 million cable and satellite subscribers in the western United States.
